image_description: A museum display featuring a large Triceratops skull fossil in the foreground, characterized by three horns and a large frill. In the background, partially obscured by glass reflections and the skull, is a mounted skeleton of another dinosaur (likely a hadrosaur or similar) and a human observer wearing a blue shirt. A text panel is visible on the left wall.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fossil skull clearly displays the iconic triceratops morphology with two large supraorbital horns and one smaller nasal horn.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a fossilized bone specimen; the keratinous beak tissue is not preserved, so this feature cannot be visually verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image primarily shows the skull. The body of the Triceratops is not present in the frame (only a different dinosaur's skeleton is in the background).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large, solid bony frill is clearly visible extending behind the eye sockets and horns.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears solid (non-fenestrated) consistent with Triceratops, and marginal undulations are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: As a bare fossil skull, no skin or scale impressions are visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The Triceratops body/limbs are not visible in the image.
The tail is not visible in the image.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The text on the museum label is illegible and distorted, appearing as gibberish characters rather than readable font, typical of AI generation or low-resolution synthesis artifacts.

The background dinosaur skeleton and the human figure exhibit warped geometry and 'melting' into the environment. The ribs/spines of the background skeleton blend unnaturally into the blue shirt of the person.

The texture of the fossil bone is somewhat uniform and plasticky, lacking the fine micro-fractures and porous detail expected in high-resolution fossil photography, though this may also be due to image resolution.
